articleTitle: Mechanical Design of a Novel Surgical Laparoscopic Simulator for Telemedicine Assistance and Physician Training during Aerospace Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Surgery in space requires enhancing the user’s skills under the expert physician's remote guidance. Therefore, the Surgical Engineering Society, with Bioastronautics and Space Mechatronics Research Group have worked on a collaborative study from 2020 to 2021, resulting in the proposed project named "SP-LAP" which is a Medical Robot, defined as a Surgical Laparoscopic Simulation Platform integrated with multi-degree-of-freedom (multi-DOF) system. The analysis is focused on the mechanical design, telemedicine assistance, surgical training and human factors, considering aerospace engineering fundamentals. It has been chosen to evaluate the surgical performance and to develop the technical-clinical validation tests at Mars Analog Desert.

articleTitle: A Study on Deep Reinforcement Learning Based Traffic Signal Control for Mitigating Traffic Congestion
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Traffic Congestion (TC) is a crucial problem in many urban areas, leading to extreme delays in daily lives. Intelligent traffic light control is a solution that dynamically balances the traffic duration based on different road traffic flows. Deep reinforcement learning (Deep RL) is a prevalent method to adapt traffic signal control in active environments nowadays. Many researchers recently developed deep RL-based intelligent and adaptive traffic signal control systems based on different states (e.g., speed and the position of vehicles) in a particular environment. However, deep RL has not employed the control of the traffic signal by observing traffic flow in any busy road. In this paper, we proposed a deep Q-network (DQN) method based on different traffic flow information to control the traffic signal dynamically. The simulation results show improved results in terms of the average delays of the vehicles.

articleTitle: Differencing Time Series as an Important Feature Extraction for Intradialytic Hypotension Prediction using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Intradialytic hypotension (IDH) needs a real-time early warning system. Thus, the goal of the research is to design time-series differences of the features of IDH to increase the performance of the warning system. We created two new features called the time-relevant difference. These features were calculated by the current value minus the previous three values. The result showed a sensitivity of 88.9% and a specificity of 85.1%. Using the LightGBM, the sensitivity was 73.8%, and the specificity was 67.9%. Time series differences generated new eigenvalues for the model system for training of non-RNN-type algorithms to obtain acceptable values.

articleTitle: Using Machine Learning to Analyze and Predict the Relations Between Cardiovascular Disease Incidence, Extreme Temperature and Air Pollution
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Due to climate change, there have been many studies on the relationship between environmental factors and diseases in recent years. Due to the characteristics of multivariable, nonlinear, sequential, continuous, and delayed effects of meteorological data, we used the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model of machine learning and the dataset from National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD) to establish a model predicting the trend of cardiovascular disease (CVD) incidence from 2009 to 2013. The best mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) was 10.98%. This predictive model helps medical institutions make appropriate medical decisions about human resource management and material scheduling, benefit clinical health education, disease prevention, as well as provide suggestions for epidemiology, environmental health, and national health policies.

articleTitle: On the Study of Smart Medical Care System Working in Senior Citizens Housing and Nursing Homes
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: This research integrates the KNRm core controller with the care system and uses the existing sensors to control the service robot to simulate the intelligent care monitoring system in the elderly care institution and the care center, control the service robot to walk, and detect the location of the elderly in Taiwan. It automatically dodges obstacles during the patrol process. The LED light is on when the infrared body sensor detects a person, and the smoke sensor detects a high concentration and makes a sound. The system immediately sends Line messages to the management through IFTT. The room uses Bluetooth control to make various movements, monitors in real-time through the network through the camera, and displays the image on the remote user's web page. The status of the nursing home through is monitored through various sensors at any time. In addition, the establishment of a notification system for elderly people falls and emergency rescues improves the quality of care for elderly people in Senior Citizens Housing and Nursing Homes.

articleTitle: Image Classification of Cassava Leaf Disease Based on Residual Network
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: For the low efficiency of the traditional visual inspection and diagnosis method for cassava leaf disease detection by agricultural experts, this paper proposes an image classification method of cassava leaf disease based on residual network (ResNet). Based on the residual network model, the idea of attention mechanism is applied to the network model, which makes the feature extraction area focus on the feature of cassava leaf disease.

articleTitle: Analysis of EMG Based Emotion Recognition for Multiple People and Emotions
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: The human-machine interaction has limitations in recognizing emotions. Electromyogram (EMG) based emotion recognition is prominent. The lack of online availability of people’s EMG signal databank constraints in research works. This research generates an EMG signal databank of nine emotions for eleven people. Long and Short Term Memory classifier (LSTM) is used for EMG-based emotion recognition. LSTM classifier achieved a 51.77% improvement in classification accuracy than Least-Square Support Vector Machine (LSSVM) classifier.

articleTitle: An Edge-Based Resource Allocation Optimization for the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT)
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: As the number of Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) increases, the need for performing on-premises tasks within hospitals or medical centers also increases. Many healthcare organizations are progressively embracing or adopting an edge computing paradigm such that computationally intensive tasks can be processed at the edge of the network in order to avoid latency and network reliability issues associated with offloading tasks to the cloud. The problem, however, hospitals or medical centers may not be equipped with sufficient computing resources that can process advanced ML or AI tasks efficiently. In addition, some tasks may not be easily offloadable or contain sensitive patient healthcare data which increases the risks of having malicious attacks. In this paper, we extend our Edgify resource provisioning framework to consider the task offloading of healthcare applications' involving patients' data as a multiple criteria decision making (MCDM) process that often involves multiple conflicting criteria (e.g. data privacy risks, costs, latency, network reliability, among others). We evaluate our proposed framework through a number of experiments which demonstrate the usefulness and effectiveness of employing our optimization approach within hospitals or medical centers.

articleTitle: Crop Disease Detection by Image Processing Using Modified Alexnet
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: This paper proposed an intelligent plant disease detection system that uses the modified Alexnet. As a convolutional neural network (CNN), Alexnet is good at objection detection from images. However, plant disease detection by the leaf image is a difficult task compared to traditional object detection. Therefore, Alexnet is modified for the different size images and angles to fit the requirement of a practical scenario. A training corpus gathered from the internet and with human leveling is used to train the detection models. According to the experimental results, the proposed approach achieves a good performance.

articleTitle: Apply LoRa Technology to Construct an Air Quality Monitoring IoT System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: This paper presents a real-time air quality monitoring system based on several LoRa sensor nodes to implement an Internet of Things (IoT) network. By using multiple sensor nodes with Arduino as the main control board, environmental parameters were collected, and the integrated data was uploaded to the cloud through a single device. Users only need to connect the gateway device to WiFi to synchronize the data of several sensor nodes in the entire system in the cloud. The device shows the air quality data of a huge area such as a campus, and users check the system data through the mobile APP and related cloud website, which includes various parameters i.e., PM1, PM2.5, PM10, temperature, and humidity.

articleTitle: Improve the Indoor Air Quality Based on Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: This study used sensors to monitor indoor carbon dioxide (CO2) concentration and fine particulate matter (PM 2.5) concentrations. Air purification equipment was run automatically to improve indoor ventilation when PM 2.5 and CO2 concentrations reach a certain level. In this paper, the Internet of Things (IoT) technology was used to upload monitoring data to the Internet. Besides, an APP was developed, which allows users to monitor air quality on mobile devices instantly. This system improved the indoor air quality of the case condition. The result implies that the smart ventilation system can lower the concentration of indoor pollutions and affect energy consumption. In addition, it will help to ensure the prevention of allergic rhinitis and respiratory diseases. That is the main contribution of this paper.

articleTitle: Semi-supervised Gastrointestinal Lesion Segmentation using Adversarial Learning
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Accurate segmentation of lesions from gastrointestinal (GI) images is vital for diagnosis and treatment management. However, with the large variability of GI images, it is challenging to enhance GI image lesion segmentation accuracy with small and many unlabeled data. Therefore, this study proposes a semi-supervised lesion segmentation using adversarial learning, which utilized limited labeled and large unlabeled images to train the model. The proposed model is evaluated on GI images from four different sources and by five segmentation evaluation metrics. Finally, the proposed model performs the mean values of segmentation accuracy (DSC=88.56±4.02, IoU=79.69±6.23, Pre=91.55±4.95, Rec=86.07±5.89, and HD=24.85±15.71), which is better than that of existing related works. Thus, a good computer-aided diagnosis system is constructed based on the proposed model for improving accuracy and minimize clinical burdens.

articleTitle: Numerical prediction for Systolic Blood Pressure in Intradialytic Hypotension Using Time-relevant RNN Models
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: During hemodialysis (HD), intradialytic hypotension (IDH) is a serious complication and a major risk factor of mortality. This study aimed to use machine learning to predict IDH occurrence to improve prevention. In the proposed model in this study, we conducted Gated Recurrent Units, Deep Neural Networks, and Long-Short-term Memory models to predict SBP values. For predicting IDH, a binary classification model was established. The results showed an accuracy of 90% with a difference between the predicted and actual value of 25mm- Hg for SBP value prediction. Also, the binary classification model had a threshold of 90mm-Hg with a accuracy of 93% and a specificity of 97%.

articleTitle: An AMDOCT-NET for Automated AMD Detection under Evaluations of Different Image Size, Denoising and Cropping
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: This paper proposed a novel deep learning architecture, called the AMDOCT-NET architecture, to accurately detect age-related macular degeneration (AMD) on optical coherence tomography (OCT) images. Using the AMDOCT-NET architecture, the performance of various image processing, such as resizing, denoising, and cropping has been evaluated. The simulation results show that the AMDOCT-NET architecture with an input size of 224×224 pixels, no cropping, and no denoising achieves the accuracy of 99.09% to automatically detect the AMD. Compared with the well-known deep learning architecture, VGG16, the AMDOCT-NET improves accuracy by 2.09% and reduces the model size by 53.7%.

articleTitle: Evaluation of an Intelligent Edge Computing System for the Hospital Intensive Care Unit
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: The evolution of medical technology along with information and communication technologies has accelerated the development and operationalization of smart hospitals recently. Traditionally, such hospitals typically rely on cloud computing platforms for data treatment and processing. However, the expansion and popularization of Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices and constant data monitoring have resulted in massive amounts of generated data, leading to the overload of the cloud infrastructure. This results in high power consumption and latency in data transmission, which is critical especially in a healthcare environment where data flow must be particularly responsive. Thus, we proposed and designed a Raspberry Pi-based edge computing system to computer-intensive care unit (ICU) data at the periphery of the network to offload the hospital cloud platform. ICU medical data were simulated from the PhysioNet MIMIC III database and transferred to the edge platform for computation and identification of emergency cases that were then sent to the cloud level. We further discuss the current issues and prospects of edge computing in hospitals.

articleTitle: Interactive Mobile App for Self-Supervised Health Management
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Health management systems have always been one of the most popular systems for the public, due to the assistance they provide for the people to record their health information. A comprehensive view of existing travel planning systems has revealed that most of the relevant studies have focused on the function of recording people’s information. However, these systems do not give positive or negative feedback and suggestions based on the recorded information. As a result, many users are not clear about how to adjust their lifestyle or diet, which does not help users become healthier. In this study, we developed an interactive health management system that includes functions of recording user health information, as well as corresponding health management feedback. This feedback is used in the system to remind users of daily health management and to establish positive health management. This system greatly enhances the practicability of self-supervised health management and increases the likelihood of helping people become healthier.

articleTitle: The New Method of Feature Selection for Intradialytic Hypotension Prediction using Machine learning
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Intradialytic hypotension (IDH) is a common complication and make patient get brain and heart disease. This study aimed to use the new method of feature selection to improve the performance of IDH prediction. We used feature importance by a different model to sort from high to low one by one, remove the lowest feature importance, and follow the rule again. Therefore, we obtain the combination of feature values that have the highest accuracy for predictive power. After applying REFCV with linear regression, the AUC of ROC increased to 0.966 (2-layers LSTM) and 0.965 (3-layers LSTM). The feature selection method we designed resulted in a better prediction ability in the model.

articleTitle: An Implementation and Development of Distributed Visualized Information Device via MQTT Broker Based on Internet of Thing Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: The visualized information is a critical issue of information systems, especially, instant and emergent information generated from mass devices with environmental sensing sensors distributed in living, home, factory, metropolitan, and so on. There is critical and instant information not only to be stored in the database but also visualized. Thus, the traditional techniques of information systems collect, store, summarise, and report but failed to reflect the urgency. Therefore, we try to integrate the Internet of Things and message queue telemetry transport (MQTT) to develop and implement a prototype device embedded in a tiny system to achieve instant and visualized information encapsulated in a box or shell and to support requested users with the independent and isolated device only. Thus, the devices are entitled as distributed visualized information device (DVID) that solves the instant visualized issues of the specialized information from a cloud platform, connect sensor devices, or any information system. This study uses the ESP32 microcontroller unit as a centurial-processor to integrate the dot matrix display for a large size display and a thin-film-transistor liquid-crystal display (TFT LCD) as a portable display to demonstrate the feasibility and usability of research goals. The devices connect to the cloud platform, subscribe to the MQTT Broker, and collect data to visualize the information without extra sub-system supports of the information systems to work independently.

articleTitle: Using Deep Learning Algorithms in Chest X-ray Image COVID-19 Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: We are experiencing heavy COVID-19 outbroke globally since January 2020. In Taiwan, because its low infection rate (<; 0.01%), there was not enough evidence for diagnosis through medical imaging. At present, chest X-ray is widely used in lung infection diagnoses. This study uses deep learning methods to assist doctors in classifying COVID-19 disease from chest X-ray images. After pre-processing, the images were put into the VGG16 model to automatically classify into three categories to assist the radiologist in the treatment of the disease. The results show that the classification accuracy was 78%. Detail analyses disclosed that this accuracy can be improved by rectifying the unbalanced images problem. In addition, choosing proper image pre-processing algorithms has a high tendency to generate better results.

articleTitle: A Self-Adaptive IoT-based Approach for Improving the Decision Making of Active Surgical Robots in Hospitals
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: In recent years, surgical robots have become instrumental tools for assisting surgeons in performing complex surgical procedures in hospitals. Unlike conventional surgical methods, robotic systems help surgeons, for example, to perform minimally invasive surgical procedures while enhancing the precision and control of operations (e.g. tiny incisions, wound sutures, endoscopic suturing, among others). To this extent, it is essential to consider several factors that may influence the feasibility and decision making of employing robotic systems in surgical procedures. In this paper, we propose an IoT-based self-adaptive approach that uses multi-criteria decision analysis methods (MCDA) for enhancing the decision making of operations involving surgical robots. Throughout this paper, we present experimental validation results in utilizing MCDA as an effective strategy for enhancing the decisions of employing robotic systems in surgical procedures.

articleTitle: Developing a Cloud Information Monitoring and Recommendation Multi-agent System based on Artificial Intelligence Technology for Smart Energy-saving
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Smart energy-saving is one of the important topics of applied science. Artificial intelligence (AI) is also worth paying attention to for intelligent systems. This study aimed to develop a cloud multi-agent system that integrates multiple intelligent technologies for quickly, accurately, and effectively obtaining useful cloud energy-saving information on time for applying science. The proposed system was successfully built by ontology, Web services, and big data analytic technologies based on many practical developments in the Dr. What-Info system. To build the system, we surveyed the related techniques for constructing a Web service platform and explored how to broadly combine cloud interactions among all sub-agents. The preliminary system shows that the proposed system architecture and operation have met the system design requirements.

Author Keywords: information monitoring and recommendation multi-agent systems

articleTitle: Using Internet of Things to Tackle Covid-19: A Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Internet of things technologies are increasingly used for healthcare. It is also used in a pandemic situation. A systematic review of the Internet of things to solve the Covid-19 pandemic is performed in this paper to investigate state-of-the-art. Data were extracted from 31 selected primary relevant studies of 155 found papers connected to the mentioned research theme. The main result of this work is the list of suggestions for future research related to the usage of Internet of Things technologies for contact tracing, health monitoring, social distance enforcement, and similar applications use to handle the Covid-19 situation.

articleTitle: Using Deep Learning to Locate Lung Tumor from Chest X-ray Images
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Pneumonia is one of the top ten causes of death. Early diagnosis of pneumonia is essential for subsequent effective treatment. Judging from the current development situation, many effective artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms are concentrated on diseases with a large amount of standardized data. After all, to achieve high-quality AI diagnosis, a large number of high-quality annotated images are required for pre-algorithm training.This research uses semi-supervised learning with Tensorflow and keras two frameworks to construct a disease location system. We use VGG16 and establish a deep convolutional generation confrontation network (DCGAN) [1], synthesize chest X-ray data, and amplify the data set. With an improved visualization effect, a heat map is used to display the lesions to assist clinical medical care personnel to fully grasp the patient's condition. We show examples of CAMs on the pneumonia detection task with no augmentation and DCGAN. It can be concluded that DCGAN performs the best results, the accuracy rate was increased by 11%.

articleTitle: An Implementation and Development of Information Delivery for PID Controller Based on Internet of Thing
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: For many small and medium-sized enterprises and small factories in Taiwan, Proportional-Integral-Derivative Controller (PID) Controller is widely used in factory equipment. This equipment is simple, stable, cheap, useful, and operating with high cost-performance all year round. For decades, these PID Controllers have been working uninterrupted on the production line for the factory automation revolution. We try to integrate the industrial internet of things and message queue telemetry transport protocol (MQTT) to establish a two-way information acquisition and remote PID controller settings to upgrade their capabilities painless. The entire PID controller upgrades to access the clouding platform which is centrally controlled and provided for top managers or decision-makers such as operators, production managers, business managers, equipment maintainers, and decision managers at any time. Mobile devices and the Internet enable the far-reaching remote setting and monitoring of the upgraded PID controllers. This study uses the microprocessor to access Wi-Fi wireless network, connect to the PID controller via RS-485 wiring and Modbus communication protocol, and then communicate with the PID controllers. Based on communication commands, the controllers retrieve the settings of the devices and the sensors with the mechanism of connecting Internet via Access Point (AP). Thus, they are upgraded to powerful wireless PID controllers.

articleTitle: Recording breathing volumes with magnetic motion sensors, dedicated to COPD during the CPT session
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: COPD is the third leading cause of death worldwide. Such pathologies require airway clearance methods implemented during CPT sessions. Monitoring breathing volumes during a session could provides the understanding of the techniques, as well as the time tracking of obstructions. Spirometry and thoracic movement measurements are performed on healthy subjects thanks to a dedicated innovative device, to calculate FEV1/FVC% index. We compare the obtained results with the motion sensors with those of the spirometer using the Bland-Altman plot method. This measuring system allows monitoring the evolution of the respiratory volumes during a CPT session.

articleTitle: Vertical-Intersection-Based Top-Down Algorithm for Frequent Itemset Mining on MapReduce
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Frequent itemset mining (FIM) is a critical problem in association rule mining(ARM), sequence mining, and biomedical text summarization. Apriori-like parallel FIM algorithms scan a database multiple times and generate an excessive number of candidate itemsets for counting their frequencies. It suffers from potential problems such as high I/O traffic and a huge amount of memory usage. Dist-Eclat-like parallel FIM algorithms address the scalability problem. However, they are incapable of constructing an in-memory vertical form to accommodate a large-scale database. This paper proposes a vertical-intersection-based top-down algorithm for frequent itemset mining on MapReduce. The concept of transaction subcube is introduced as all the closed itemsets and their frequencies are derived by employing the vertical intersection method. The frequently closed itemsets are translated into frequent itemsets quickly in the top-down traveling manner with the aid of the negative form of subcubes. Thus, the proposed vertical-intersection-based algorithms have the capability of highly parallel processing, resulting in speeding up the system performance significantly.

articleTitle: Knee Exoskeleton- Review of Knee Musculature and Exoskeleton Device Proposed Design
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: A review of the lower extremity musculature surrounding the knee is provided as well as a lower extremity knee exoskeleton design proposed. The review provides a general understanding of the body m usculature around the knee with an emphasis on the geometry of the musculature. The proposed device design uses the reviewed musculature geometry as the basis for the design. In function, the proposed device focuses on creating a mechanical advantage at the knee joint which assists individuals who are suffering temporarily, or permanently, from quadriceps weakness or atrophy brought on by Osteoarthritis, Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome (PFPS), or other knee conditions. The design was analyzed over flexion angles between 0 to 90 degrees. Physical testing, as well as linear and nonlinear model calculations, were performed to determine the design’s strength capacity and function. The resulting force and momentum values of the device were compared to those characteristics of a healthy leg (a hip-to-knee length of 18 inches and a body weight of 180 pounds as the standard dimension and weight for testing). From the comparison data, the proposed device was found to be significantly similar to the body’s calculated maximum applied moment. Additionally, the comparison of the curves of the moment versus flexion angle for the device and body showed the linear model case to not be similar to the body while the nonlinear model case was similar to the body.

articleTitle: A Priority Contention Window Mechanism for Ad Hoc Network
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Ad hoc network is a no wired connection and self-configuring, self-organizing, infrastructure-free mobile network. Many studies have proposed different optimized routing protocol and various simulation to improve its performance of ad hoc network. Whatever, most of them only concentrate on the routing problems, but do not take into consideration the medium contention problems of the MAC layer. This article studies the impact of the MAC layer by simulating the transmission of ad hoc network, and a cross-layer algorithm for ad hoc network is proposed. This framework can reduce data conflicts in the MAC layer, obtaining better transmission performance in the network layer. Finally, extended simulation clarify that the “Priority Contention Window Mechanism” can achieve significant improvements compared with conventional algorithms.

articleTitle: Development and Control of Hand Exoskeleton System Using Intended Movement
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Hand motor impairment is a common disability among stroke survivors that severely affect their ability in activities of daily livings (ADLs), reducing independence and quality of life. Throughout the rehabilitation process, stroke patients able to regain partially or fully the hand motor function. However, the conventional rehabilitation process is limited by the insufficient number of therapists, labor-intensiveness, and low compliance. The objective of this study was to support the rehabilitation process and ADLs through the development of the Flexible Linkage Hand Exoskeleton Rehabilitation Robot (FLEXOR), a five fingers 3D printed prototype actuated by linear actuators. FLEXOR was controlled using intended movement to support the independent exercises and to assist the ADLs movement. An Arduino-based control system driven by electromyography (EMG) signal was developed for FLEXOR. The new control system protected the hand against over-flexing and excessive application of force. The control system was programmed into three different operating modes which enable FLEXOR to provide passive exercises to the fingers, assist fingers in ADLs movement with minimal efforts, and provide active exercises while assisting fingers in ADLs.

articleTitle: Developing A Parser Framework based on OpenPose Skeleton Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a field of research and interest has been around for quite a long time. With the current state of technology, AI has been utilized in various fields, such as vehicle automation in the automotive, disease preliminary detection in medical, and cybersecurity in information technology. Spatial recognition has become popular owing to the rapid hike in computing power and as a result, real-world applications are starting to appear. In developed countries around the world, particularly those upgraded from developing nations, all faced the problem of the aging population. Based on the lack of frameworks available when using a state-of-the-art pose estimation of OpenPose, the research looks into building a framework to lower the bar of entering the utilization of OpenPose, thus creating opportunities for people without knowledge on data preparation. The framework used by a group of high schoolers proved the ease of access useful for the relative tech-illiterate group and bridging the gap between them and the higher education.

articleTitle: Development of Low-voltage Urine Sample Conductivity Measurement System for Kidney Stone Risk Assessment
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a 3.3 V electrical conductivity (EC) measurement system as a part of multiple parameters urine test equipment. The platform serves as a portable point-of-care (POC) device to collect and analysis of data from urine samples for assessing the risk of kidney stone formation. The preliminary test using potassium chloride standard solution and urine sample shows an accuracy of 5% in the range between 0.1 and 35mS/cm. The on-chip implementation is realized in a 0.18um CMOS process in the future.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Usage of Oil Palm Harvesting Tools on Work Related Musculoskeletal Disorders of Lower Limb
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Worker’s health and safety are important for the plantation’s sustainable development. In the oil palm industry, the harvester is exposed to work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) during the fresh fruit bunch (FFB) harvesting process. The objective of this study was to investigate the effect of harvesting tools namely chisel, pole, and loading spike towards WMSDs on harvester’s lower limb. Rapid Upper Limb Analysis (RULA) in the CATIA and Human Musculoskeletal Model Analysis (HMMA) in the AnyBody software was applied to model and simulate the harvester’s movement during the harvesting process. The RULA simulation results indicated that the harvester’s lower limbs were exposed to WMSDs where further investigation and changes were required immediately. HMMA results indicated that the Gastrocnemius Medialis muscle had the highest mean muscle force. This study is important as an early ergonomics intervention for occupational health.

articleTitle: Pipelined ADC in Parallel and Low Noise Amplifier Design for Neural Recording Device
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: This article introduces a 20-bit pipelined analog to digital converter and low noise amplifier with a wake-up receiver from an RF detector in a double-sided stacked-up integrated circuit as a neural recording device. The proposed design is to obtain stable built-in action and local field potential. The optimized phase margin of ideal degrees is made sure as compared with original solutions. This article introduces a solution for early diagnoses by establishing a neural recording architecture to measure electroencephalography (EEG) signal along with a deep neural network (DNN) that classify the suspected patients.

articleTitle: An Exploration of Online Teaching Based on Arduino Virtual Simulation Experiments
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: In offline teaching, there are problems such as high cost and consumption of hardware and irreversible operation in training, which cause difficulties in actual running offline. Through a teaching test by online virtual simulation experiments, this study found that the environment, contents, requirements, methods,procedures, and operationn process of experiments truly reflected the process of hardware experiments, and motivate users to participate.

articleTitle: Influential Components for the Sustainability of IoT-enabled Smart Systems: A Hierarchical Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: The IoT-enabled smart systems provide convenience to users but also raise issues about sustainability. So far, studies in the sustainability of IoT-enabled smart systems are relatively scant. This research thus examines critical components which influence the sustainability of IoT-enabled smart systems. An empirical study was performed using the DEMATEL method with data collected from industry experts. The results proposed the causes and effects of the factors influencing smart system sustainability. Research implications and suggestions are then elaborated.

articleTitle: EEG-based Drowsiness Detection from Ocular Indices Using Ensemble Classification
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: One of the reasons for fatal road accidents is sleeping behind the wheel, and there are numerous methods developed to prevent these accidents. The proposed method uses a MATLAB-based BLINKER algorithm to extract ocular characteristics from EEG signals. The classification model makes this method unique to detect drivers' drowsiness using eye blinks. The decision tree model is used in feature selection and a Bayesian optimized ensemble bagged classifier for the prediction. The predictive classification model gives 88.1% accuracy.

articleTitle: Comments on a Three-factor Anonymous User Authentication Scheme for Internet of Things Environments
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: IoT (Internet of Things) consists of various devices such as cars, electrical appliances, machines, and sensors. With IoT technologies, devices exchange information through the network, people are allowed to obtain information collected by devices without interacting with them, and automatic operations for devices are realized. Owing to the variety of IoT devices, some of them possess limited computational capability. On the other hand, data transmission in IoT networks is usually through a public channel. To ensure efficiency and security in IoT environments, Lee et al. presented a three-factor authentication scheme with XOR operation and hash function. Their scheme possessed superior properties and prevented common attacks. Analyzing the scheme revealed that five flaws threaten the scheme. This paper shows how the flaws threaten the scheme in detail.

articleTitle: Applying Big Data of Geographic Information to Analyze the Accessibility of Elderly Care Institutions
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: With the acceleration of aging in society, elderly care institutions have become more important in urban planning and public service facilities than before. Geographic Information System(GIS), the kernel density analysis method, and the hot spot analysis method were used to analyze the points of interest(POI) data of elderly care institutions in Baiyun District, Guangzhou in 2021. The spatial distribution and agglomeration characteristics of elderly care institutions were explored in the research area. The result provided a comprehensive spatial evaluation of the elderly care institutions and showed the following: (1) The elderly care institutions in Baiyun District exhibit the characteristics of continuous clustering and spatial distribution in multiple centers and (2) Baiyun District has the characteristics of the concentrated distribution of significant hotspots, larger clustered block types appear, and the agglomeration characteristics are obvious. The research results are used as a reference for the government to plan public service facilities for the elderly.

articleTitle: Effects of Incorporating AR-based Mobile Learning System on Elementary School Students’ Perceived Usefulness of M-learning
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: The rapid development of information technology has diversified the application of multimedia in education. Through the combination of mobile apps and augmented reality (AR) technology, smart devices such as tablet computers and smartphones make learning interesting and enable diverse interaction modes. The starting point of this study was creative teaching covering topics such as ecological conservation and environmental education. We created an AR app for users in schools to take an ecological tour of the plants in the diet of butterflies. The app formed the localized and special mobile learning content in school. Students were allowed to walk out of the classroom and use their mobile devices to engage in autonomous learning and determined their acceptance of the AR app.

articleTitle: Development of Microneedle Patches for Insulin Delivery
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Diabetes is a leading cause of disability and death. Moreover, it has a huge social and economic impact. Patients with diabetes have a better quality of life when they receive insulin properly than without it. However, some diabetic patients have trypanophobia, so they often avoid insulin injections resulting in life-threatening conditions. Therefore, this study aims to develop microneedle patches for transdermal insulin delivery to reduce pain from insulin injection and extend the shelf-life of insulin stored at room temperature. The insulin microneedle patches were fabricated by coating a mixture of insulin and polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) on plastic microneedle patches. A histological section showed that the microneedles had excellent mechanical strength to penetrate porcine cadaver skin. The stability test using the insulin Elisa kit indicated good stability of the insulin/PVA coated on the microneedle patches stored at room temperature whereas its biological activity was higher than 90% after 30 days of storage.

articleTitle: Integration of MQTT Communication and Fire Sensor for Hospital Alarm System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: As society gradually relies on technologies to prevent dangers and detect the environment, the processing of data transmission and analysis becomes important. In recent years, firefighters are sacrificed during rescue missions. Even with the high-tech equipment in the current era, the lives of firefighters are not prevented in the fire scene. Thus, this research designs and develops an alarm system for hospitals and schools. The Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) technology and fire sensors are utilized and integrated to extract the conditions of the environment. In the system, the subscriber server collects the data on a personal computer. Also, the website and database server monitor the wards in a hospital. Integrating and designing the systems help to understand the emergent situation.

articleTitle: Investigating the influence through EEG: Using Technology to Introduce Cognitive Training for Patients with Mild Dementia
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Many researchers have pointed out that cognitive training can improve the cognitive function of patients with dementia. Therefore, our research developed a digital cognitive application system, "Reminiscence", to observe the brainwave of patients with dementia through cognitive training and to analyze its influence on concentration, memory, and logic. In this study, a total of 16 patients with mild dementia (CDR 0.5 and 1) participated in the measurement of brainwave by using the NeuroSky EEG system in the digital cognitive nostalgia system. The cognitive training is divided into seven parts: photo sharing, song singing, questions in logic, number operation, jigsaw puzzle, weight identification, and silhouette puzzle. Among the seven question types of cognitive training in this experiment, the six items of photo sharing, song singing, questions in logic, number operation, jigsaw puzzle, weight identification, and silhouette puzzle had a good impact on dementia patients and helped their concentration. The improvement of memory and logic had a positive effect on the delay of cognitive function degradation of patients with dementia. The purpose of this study is to stimulate and improve the cognitive function of patients with dementia, thus delaying dementia. This research serves as a reference for the future development of technology-assisted applications for patients with dementia who need cognitive training.

articleTitle: FBS-based One-bit Precoding Scheme for Large-scale Multi-antenna Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Spatial modulation (SM) is an important multi-antenna transmission technique. By encoding the data with additional spatial information, the spectral efficiency is enhanced without extra bandwidth. By extending the SM concept to the multiple-user in a massive multiple-input multiple-output (MU-M-MIMO) scenario, only one radio frequency (RF) is needed in the transmitter (Tx), which improves the energy efficiency. To further reduce the cost and power consumption, one-bit digitalto-analog converters (DACs) are adopted in the Tx RF chain at the expense of high precoding complexity to compensate the severe performance degradation caused by the nonlinear one-bit quantization distortion. In this paper, a low-complexity precoding scheme based on the forward-backward splitting (FBS) method is presented for the large-scale multi-antenna system with SM and quadrature-phase-shift-keying (QPSK) signaling. Preliminary simulation results show that, comparing to the other one-bit DAC based benchmark methods, the proposed precoder is able to achieve the same (or better) BER at a much lower computational complexity.

articleTitle: Lower Limbs EMG Signal Analysis for Bottom Group of Muscles Fitness Norm Before and After Intensive Exercise
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Physical fitness refers to the body's ability to adapt to work and environment, as well as the ability to function in physical behavior. This research is based on physical fitness, from the viewpoint of exercise physiology, muscle strength, muscle endurance, and muscle power, to quantitatively study physical fitness. In this study, standing long jump was used as a normal physical fitness test, and the lowest 20% group were screened from university freshmen. After intensive exercise training, the pre-and post-test results were analyzed under different intensities. A correlation between its time and frequency domain characteristics and muscle fitness was found, too. The subjects performed four different exercise intensities (No Load, 8RM, 18RM, 28RM) and plate experiments with weight-bearing squats. Their EMG signals during exercise were recorded for time and frequency domain analysis and analyzed by using the paired sample t-test to find the difference of the characteristic index of the lowest group under different exercise intensities. The research results show that after intensive training, RMS has significant differences in the 8RM exercise experiment, while MAV, VAR, and AAC do in the 18RM exercise experiment. Several time-domain indicators (RMS, AAC) and frequency domain indicators (MNF, MDF) have significant differences in the 18RM exercise experiment. MAV, VAR, RMS, and AAC have significant differences in the 28RM exercise experiment.

articleTitle: Finger Induced Auto-Thermogenesis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Heat through hand-clasping with a specific finger pose (HCFP) is a tool for eliciting innate immune system response to control the SARs-CoV-2 virus. Fifteen male subjects participate in a study in which ECG and axillary temperature are measured, with and without HCFP. The heat induction is derived from temperature slope and we studied its effect on heart rate variability (HRV) and resting metabolic rate (RMR). Compared to the normal state, the average axillary temperature slope increases by 11.5% along with a significant increase in resting metabolic rate (RMR) (p<0.05) respectively. HRV enhances through an increase in SDRR and RMSSD by 23.75 and 24.44%, respectively. The Augmented-LFHF ratio reduces significantly (p<0.001). HCFP induces body-heat mediated by parasympathetic nervous system (PSNS) dominance with minimal changes in body temperature due to thermoregulation.

Index Terms: Response Of The Innate Immune System

articleTitle: Simulation of HIL Analog Power Meter Connection Technology for Vehicle Autonomous Driving
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: This research uses PreScan simulation software as a test platform. The vehicle's hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) links to virtual scenes and reality sensors, which reduce costs in a virtual road environment. In this study, we monitor the analog power meter on the drive shaft of the PreSan car to monitor its torque, tire rotation speed, acceleration, and design the transmission format of the power meter. The remote monitoring is standardized, as the network interface is integrated into the car computer while retaining the high reliability of the industrial-grade Ethernet network. The system meets the strict functional safety requirements of car manufacturers and Tier 1 original equipment manufacturers (OEMs). The advanced driving assistance system (ADAS) of the car allows 1) the monitoring of the analog power meter of the Ethernet to become the mainstream data collection channel, 2) the processor of the on-board system to monitor the value and communication in real-time, and 3) drive the car to check the driving condition. Through the development of PreScan, intermediate monitoring and communication are completed, and the development speed is accelerated.

articleTitle: Stability Improvements of Newly-Developed Planar Brain-PET Scanner
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Due to the photonic elements sensitive to their operating temperature, the outputs of two imaging heads of a lab-developed PET scanner varied with ambient temperature fluctuation. It led to a 10% photonics gain variation and made resultant position and energy estimations drifting, thus made the prebuilt cLUT and eLUT unusable. This eventually jeopardizes the imaging process. Therefore, the conventional air- convection type heat transfer mechanism was replaced with a newly developed heat conductive and active heat control system. With the application of the new heat control system, the experienced (inner temperature of two imaging heads) temperature difference of 3–5°C (from day time to night time) reduced to 0.2°C. The test results show that the new active heat control system successfully stabilizes the imaging heads outputs and thus makes the planar brain-PET scanner capable of achieving its purpose.

articleTitle: The Sustainability Efficiency Measurement in Network DEA with Slacks-based Measures
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Environmental degradation and resource scarcity have encouraged sustainable resource utilization and environmental protection worldwide. Eco-efficiency has been considered as an indicator for sustainability analysis for the empirical relation in economic activities between environmental impact and cost. Most methods for evaluating eco-efficiencies of enterprises and industries involve subjective factors while determining weights of indicators. To address the issue, a slacks-based measure for the sustainability efficiency evaluation is proposed in this work by considering undesirable factors. The overall efficiency is derived as the weighted average of sub-system efficiencies. The study of the environmental sustainability performance of the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development countries is included. The most influential factor that causes the low environmental sustainability scores of the whole system is identified.

articleTitle: Applying fuzzy Delphi Method to Construct Evaluation Criteria for Online English Teaching
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: After the outbreak of COVID-19, traditional offline teaching is not carried out normally. However, education cannot be stopped. In this case, many teachers are facing challenges, not subject to geographical restrictions, diverse ways, and other advantages. Thus, online teaching has become an important teaching method in this special period. Based on the literature review, this paper summarizes the evaluation criteria of different levels of online English teaching. Using the questionnaire survey, experts and scholars were consulted for several rounds. After the validity of the questionnaire by using a fuzzy Delphi method, the evaluation criteria system of English online teaching was established, and the importance, order, and grade of the evaluation criteria were evaluated. This system allows teachers to formulate teaching strategies to optimize and improve English online teaching. The findings of this paper shed some light on efficient learning strategies and ensure the effect of online English teaching.

articleTitle: A Legacy Infrastructure-based Mechanism for Moving Target Defense
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: With the advancement of network technology, more electronic devices have begun to connect to the Internet. The era of IoE (Internet of Everything) is coming. However, the number of serious incidents of cyberattacks on important facilities has gradually increased at the same time. Security becomes an important issue when setting up plenty of network devices in an environment. Thus, we propose an innovative mechanism of the Moving Target Defense (MTD) to solve the problems happening to other MTD mechanisms in the past. This method applies Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) to dynamically change the IPv4 address of information equipment in the medical environment. In other words, each of the nodes performs IP-Hopping and effectively avoids malicious attacks. Communication between devices relies on DNS lookup. The mechanism avoids problems such as time synchronization and IP conflict. Also, it greatly reduces the costs of large-scale deployment. All of these problems are encountered by other MTD mechanisms in the past. Not only can the mechanism be applied to the medical and information equipment, it can also be applied to various devices connected to the Internet, including Industrial Control System (ICS). The mechanism is implemented in existing technologies and prevents other problems, which makes it easy to build a system.

articleTitle: Aluminum Oxide Thin Film Passivation Prepared by VHF-PEALD and Its Application of Light-Induced µm-Particle Screening Biochip
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: This paper proposed a biochip that uses the aluminum oxide (Al<inf>2</inf>O<inf>3</inf>) thin film passivation on the photoconductive layer surface. The Al<inf>2</inf>O<inf>3</inf> thin film was deposited by a high frequency (40.68 MHz) plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (VHF-PEALD) system to improve the photoconductive layer performance of the biochip. The proposed Al<inf>2</inf>O<inf>3</inf> thin film was measured and investigated by UV-visible spectroscopy (UV-Vis), atomic force microscope (AFM), transmission electron microscope (TEM), and I-V curve. An Al<inf>2</inf>O<inf>3</inf> thin film was deposited on the surface of the photoconductive layer to provide a smooth surface. Using a proposed 14 nm Al<inf>2</inf>O<inf>3</inf> thin film passivation on the 550 nm, the photoconductive layer effectively reduces the surface roughness from 8.47 to 6.87 nm. The biochip with Al<inf>2</inf>O<inf>3</inf> thin film passivation on photoconductive layer has better performance than conventional biochip. The maximum manipulation velocity of particles increased by 35%, and the screening efficiency was up to 80%. This method provides high-efficiency light-induced dielectrophoresis biochips.

articleTitle: The Use of IgY (Immunoglobulin Yolk) in Cancer Prevention Seen in Liver and Stomach Cancers
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Cancer is the number one death causing disease in the world. The best way for cancer treatment is prevention. Certain cancers such as liver and stomach cancers occur due to certain infectious agents. Stomach cancer is linked to the bacterial Helicobacter pylori (H. Pylori) infection, and liver cancer is linked to hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV). In our clinical trial, animals treated with IgY (Immunoglobulin Yolk) showed increased natural killer (NK) cell killing activity and IFN-r, which further helped the body’s immune system to kill the virus including HBV and HCV. Our clinical results show that that IgY products can indeed reduce the viral counts in Hepatitis B and C. H. Pylori can cause peptic ulcers, chronic active gastritis and gastric malignancies. Specific IgY can catch the H. Pylori bacteria, remove them from stomach, and reduce gastric malignancies. In conclusion, IgY can be utilized in the prevention of liver and stomach cancer.

articleTitle: A Vertical-Location Metric Based on Characteristics of Barometric Pressure Sensors
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: This article presents a vertical-location approach based on characteristics of barometric pressure sensors (BPSs), where the altitude information of mobile devices is measured and extracted from BPSs based on microelectromechanical systems. On account of environmental factors about atmospheric pressure changes and quantization noises, the calibration approaches are proposed to compute the height information about z-axis and to compensate for the offset difference between BPSs. The experimental results demonstrate that the vertical-location accuracy of the proposed approach can be used for the applications of location-based services.

articleTitle: Influence of Inclined Magnetic Field on Heat Transfer Transitions of Nanofluids Flow
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: In this paper, numerical simulations are carried out on steady natural convection of Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O nanofluids within a square enclosure, and the interaction effects of an inclined magnetic field and heat transfer behaviors are investigated. The Buongiorno’s two-phase mixed model is adopted with two slip mechanisms: thermophoresis and Brownian diffusion. The heat transfer transition is first detected by increasing nanoparticle volume fraction for various Rayleigh numbers. Effects of magnetic intensity and magnetic declination are further investigated. It is found that the critical Rayleigh number changes nonlinearly with the increase of the inclined angle, and the heat transfer deduces with the raise of the magnetic strength. The relationship between the heat transfer rates and the magnetic inclination is dominated by the strength of magnetic field, where the distribution changes from asymmetric mode to symmetric mode with the growth of magnetic intensity.

articleTitle: How Older Adults’ User Experiences of Smart Healthcare System are Affected by their Cultural Differences
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Population aging is a challenging and cross-culture problem throughout the world. At present, developing smart healthcare systems is a critical way to help realize healthy aging. On the other hand, the integration of data acquisition modules in multiple non-invasive sensors and wireless local area networks makes it possible to timely find and detect health problems in older adults. This study aims at exploring the influence of older adults' culture differences on user experience design for the smart healthcare system. This paper also suggests that the user experience design of the smart healthcare system needs to be carried out based on a concrete analysis of older adults' cultural life to improve the health and wellbeing of older adults in their later years.

articleTitle: Effects of Increased Catheter Contact Force on the Ablation Impedance in the Radiofrequency Catheter Ablation of Cardiac Arrhythmias
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Catheter contact force is well known as one of the factors which has a strong positive correlation with lesion formation. We hypothesized that the catheter contact force substantially affects the ablation impedance variation during radiofrequency (RF) catheter cardiac ablation, due to its direct effect on the electrical current output from the RF generator. However, such a hypothesis needs to be validated through further investigation. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to understand the effect of the catheter contact force related to the contact angle on the ablation impedance in the radiofrequency catheter cardiac ablation process. Thus, we developed a special in vitro experimental system that enables to precisely set the catheter contact angle to the heart tissue's surface. The catheter ablation test was held at five different contact angles to the heart tissue surface. A RF current was delivered at each angle at contact force values of 2, 4, 6, 10, 15, 20, 30, and 40 gf. RF catheter ablation examination was repeated six times each for the five levels of contact angles and eight levels of contact forces. Then, the maximum impedance and average impedance during the ablation process for each condition were recorded. The results revealed that the catheter contact force has a significant correlation with ablation impedance. When the contact force was increased, the different impedance between the maximum impedance and average impedance also increased. The percentage of contact area also has a significant correlation with the ablation impedance. When the percentage of contact area was increased, the different impedance between the maximum and the average impedance also increased. However, the ablation impedance did not have a significant difference with each catheter contact angle. The present study showed a significant impact of the catheter contact force on the ablation impedance in RF catheter ablation systems.

articleTitle: A Design of Circuit Break Detector for a P-type Fire Detector Central Control
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Fire detector central controls installed in present buildings of Taiwan belong to the P-type. All fire alarm sensors in the same zone are connected to the same circuit. On-site inspectors cannot confirm the source of the fire as a fire occurs and the circuit is disconnected. There is also no way of distinguishing which detector is out of service in the event of a fire alarm as the disconnected circuit causes detectors to be disabled. The on-site inspector does not respond in time. That is the main cause of increased fire damage. In practice, the detection of circuit disconnection must be carried out by fire practitioners using ladders or scaffolds to measure the circuit voltage of all detectors on the circuit. In addition to increasing maintenance costs with high floors, it also increases the risk of inspectors falling from heights. Therefore, this study provides a fire alarm disconnection detector of a P-type fire detector control. We designed an extension rod equipped with a 1 kHz, 10 V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p-p</inf> AC signal audio transmitter/receiver for preventing the fire alarm the disconnected circuit, connecting to the audio transmitter, and using the extension rod to detect all detectors that are disconnected on the circuit to reduce the danger of fire practitioners during the detection and improve the detection efficiency.

articleTitle: Constructing the Seniors Learns XR Innovative Night Market Play Situation with ARCS Theory
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Aging accompanies inconvenience and physical deterioration, such as forgetfulness, declining hands and feet, and chronic diseases. To improve the physical function of the seniors, this study uses the innovative night market play into the interactive situation of extended reality as the basis for development. The motivation theory triggers the seniors to learn an innovative night market play situation that brings pleasure and laughter. The result shows that the situation of the XR night market makes the physical and psychological aspects of the seniors achieve health goals, and the images generated by the interactive situations also enable the seniors to have leisure fun.

articleTitle: An Image Recognition-based Distance Measurement Technique for Real-time Locating of Construction Workers
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Real-time location of construction workers is crucial information for site safety management as the construction accidents usually happen instantly when the workers are facing dangerous hazards. Previous methods for developing Real-time Locating System (RTLS) are either imprecise enough or too expensive for practical applications. This paper presents an Image Recognition-based Distance Measurement Technique that achieved 2.13% average error rate or 15 cm distance error. It outperforms other RTLS techniques including RFID, GPS, VA, WLAN, and is close to NFC and UWB but much more cost-effective and easily implemented.

articleTitle: Health Warning Scheme Based on Image Recognition with Garmin Connect Mobile App
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: This paper proposed a health warning system to effectively help individuals or companies fetch the significant parameter of sleep deficiency, protect privacy, and further decrease related accidents due to a person's sleep deficiency. Significantly, it benefits public safety in major industries such as agriculture, manufacturing, and services. This system employs face recognition and optical character recognition for the individual identity and daily sleep time from the daily health report of the Garmin Connect mobile app on the user's smartphone screen.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Hydrogen Production Trends with Porosity of the Electrode of URSOFC
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: A regenerative solid oxide fuel cell model under multi-physics coupling was built to study the influence of different design parameters on fuel cell performance. First, the hydrogen production performance increases slightly when the cathode porosity increases from 0.2 to 0.4. However, there is no significant difference in the hydrogen production performance when the cathode porosity increases from 0.4 to 0.6. The influence of the average cathode pore size on the hydrogen production performance is limited.

articleTitle: A Study on Training Course for Staffs to Solve Expertise Issues with Multiple Criteria Decision Making Methodology – a Case of PC-based Information Security Monitoring Tool Development
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: The development of a PC-based information security monitoring tool (PISMT) involves what events are required to monitor and what information is needed to collect. For developing staff, there is a multiple criteria issue. This study proposed a multiple criteria decision making (MCDM) process method (MCDMPM) to explore a PC-based information security monitoring tool (PISMT) development. The MCDMPM trains the developing staff to determine which functionalities receive implementation priorities in a PISMT. The MCDMPM adopted a literature survey, Delphi, and AHP to explore a PISMT development. First, the MCDMPM taught the developing staff to launch a thorough literature survey to have concise operational definitions for each functionality, which might implement in an ISMT. Second, the MCDMPM trained the staff to establish and confirm a criteria decision hierarchy with the Delphi method. Third, the MCDMPM assisted the staff to investigate the individual opinions of the experts using AHP. Finally, based on the individual opinions of the experts, the MCDMPM taught the staff to receive aggregated group opinions for each functionality under each construct/the total goal. With the result of the PISMT development, the developing staff implemented significant functionalities for development effectiveness. The empirical evidence for the effectiveness of the MCDMPM is shown from the PISMT development.

articleTitle: Effect of Alpha Wave-Containing Music on the Psychological Stress Level of Hospital Staffs and their Cognitive Performance
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: This study aims to investigate the effect of alpha music therapy that is an affordable, easily implemented, and sustainable method on stress level, cognitive functions, and physiological response of hospital staff amidst the context of the COVID-19 pandemic. The testing group was required to listen to alpha music for two weeks. Stress questionnaires, cognitive tasks, and physiological data were collected before and after the intervention. Blood pressure and heart rate between the two groups do not differ significantly and change after intervention. The increase in PSS scores and fast response time in the Matrix Task of the Control group indicate increasing stress levels, reduced attention, and remembering ability. These results of the Control group explain the high workload at the year-end and COVID-19 outbreak in Vietnam occurring during the second data collection week. In contrast, both the PSS and Respond time measures suggest a positive effect of alpha music on the Testing group.

articleTitle: Investigation on Critical Factors of Smart Green Building in the Era of the Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: In the 21st century, as the process of global development accelerates, many countries are facing problems and challenges such as resource scarcity and environmental pollution. Thus, the concept of green and sustainable development has become a major trend in the development of countries around the world. With high energy consumption, the construction industry must also adhere to the principle of green ecological sustainable development. In the emerging of the Internet of Things, green building is combined with current information technology such as big data and cloud computing to generate the new concept of smart green building, which gradually becomes the core development of the modern construction industry. This paper summarizes the critical factors of smart green building, applies a structural model with ISM interpretation, conducts the convergence analysis of key factors, and finally constructs a structural model of critical factors of smart green building. The results positively respond to China's sustainable development strategy and provide the reference for the construction of smart green buildings, thus promoting the long-term development of the smart green building industry.

articleTitle: Institutional Research: Issue-Oriented Data Integration and System Construction
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: This study proposes an issue-oriented data integration and system-building model to promote institutional research. In direction of the issues, we advance the idea of grouping university stakeholders into the university, students, and the public. In the aspect of data integration and system construction, five steps are proposed: issue confirmation, information system and data inventory, data model establishment, data warehouse and data dictionary establishment, and system construction and data analysis. Finally, this study proposes several preliminary conclusions and suggestions on the promotion of institutional research for universities or researchers.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approach for Risk Prediction of Erosive Esophagitis in a Health Check-up Population in Taiwan
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Erosive esophagitis is a kind of GERD (gastroesophageal reflux disease) that potentially develops adenocarcinoma of the esophagus. We collected the data of greater or equal to 20 undergoing upper gastrointestinal endoscopy in a health check-up center between October 2018 and December 2020. We constructed machine learning models using RF (random forest), SVM (support vector machines), MLP Classifier (multi-layer perceptron classifier), and XGBoost and compared them for cross-validation. The risk prediction model identifies high-risk individuals of EE before endoscope examination.

articleTitle: Integrating IOT, Game Engineering and Data Modeling with 2D-3D Design in Developing Virtual-Physical Interactive Cognition Game Box
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: In support of the gerontechnology development of university social responsibility for community and educational requirements, this study develops a virtual-physical interactive cognition game box for elders. After interviewing the care needs of community development association members, we propose a production prototype that combines science technology and art design with virtual-physical integration upon the considerations of technical feasibility and HCI design. The prototype was constructed by integrating the 3D shape design, laser engraving design/implementation, character design and animation, game engineering, data modeling, the internet of things (IoT), and so on. To further improve the Virtual-Physical Interactive Cognition Game Box prototype, several user experience activities were conducted in the community and the university. It has also been introduced in related courses in the form of cases integrating interdisciplinary works into virtual-physical interaction designs for students. Data engineering will be the next step in the future.

articleTitle: Policy and Value Deep RL for Temporal Language-Agnostic Street Image Captioning
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Dashcams and street cameras capture a huge amount of street and traffic video data. Temporal image captioning for such video data has been approached with an encoder-decoder framework and achieved substantial success in captioning accuracy. Most recently, policy and value deep reinforcement learning (PVRL) emerged as an outperformer over other decision-making frameworks for image captioning. In this paper, we design a framework that utilizes PVRL on an inhouse dataset containing temporal images of East Asia streets as a step towards designing a language-agnostic street image captioning framework that is capable of captioning temporal images of any street regardless of location. For language- invariance, the framework includes cross-modal retrieval at the character level so that similar words in different languages but in the same word-embedding space are grouped together. Our results show that PVRL can be applied successfully to temporal video captured the streets and achieve natural semantic captions; preliminary studies on our dataset suggest that the framework is capable of use in multi-language scenarios.

articleTitle: Renovation of Existing Residential Communities Using Green Energy Conservation Technology
