publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Nowadays, in the process of rebuilding old communities, we still face various difficulties such as financing and negotiation. One of the reasons is the lack of green retrofitting awareness of residents. This study tries to develop a green retrofitting evaluation framework that is used by the residents so that they know the renovation problems the community has encountered. Through expert interviews and literature reviews, the criteria and the sub-criteria in each criterion in the retrofitting evaluation framework were developed first. Then, the Delphi expert questionnaires were used to determine the final evaluation framework, which consisted of five criteria and eighteen sub-criteria. The five criteria were energy utilization, water use, waste minimization and recycling, public facilities, and ecology. Thereafter, the Analytic Hierarchical Process (AHP) was used to understand the importance of each obtained sub-criterion by finding its absolute weight. Finally, each factor was applied to an old community in Zhangpu County, Fujian Province, China to diagnose the renovation problems encountered and the renovation strategies were proposed using available green energy conservation technology.

articleTitle: Detecting Cyber-Attacks in Modern Power Systems Using an Unsupervised Monitoring Technique
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Cyber-attacks detection in modern power systems is undoubtedly indispensable to enhance their resilience and guarantee the continuous production of electricity. As the number of attacks is very small compared to normal events, and attacks are unpredictable, it is not obvious to build a model for attacks. Here, only anomaly-free measurements are utilized to build a reference model for intrusion detection. Specifically, this study presents an unsupervised intrusion detection approach using the k-nearest neighbor algorithm and exponential smoothing monitoring scheme for uncovering attacks in modern power systems. Essentially, the k-nearest neighbor algorithm is implemented to compute the deviation between actual measurements and the faultless (training) data. Then, the exponential smoothing method is used to set up a detection decision-based kNN metric for anomaly detection. The proposed procedure has been tested to detect cyber-attacks in a two-line three-bus power transmission system. The proposed approach has been shown good detection performance.

articleTitle: Using Big Data Analytics on Health Industry Development: The Empirical Intellectual Property Analysis from Stem Cell Therapy
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Stem cells have become indispensable in tissue engineering and regenerative medicine applications, which provides a suitable opportunity to observe stem cell therapy from technology development. This research aims to evaluate the developmental trends of the stem cell therapy industry. Results show that the diagram of mutual citation of patents provides the relationships between patent citations and specific applications via network structure. Finally, implications and developmental strategies are proposed for future cell therapy industry development.

articleTitle: Towards Mitigating Probable Road Mishaps through DQN Based Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Road accident is a widespread problem in many urban areas nowadays. Reckless Driving (Over-Speed) is one of the attributes leading to the enormous destruction of pedestrian life. Autonomous vehicle speed control is an important research area in the Intelligent Transportation System (ITS) to mitigate road accidents in densely populated areas. Many existed works utilized Reinforcement Learning (RL) to control the vehicle speed intelligently. However, controlling the over-speed of the vehicle using RL under the speed limit of the different zones (i.e., Town, Rural Main Road, Highways, and so forth) is also another demanding task because of the speed limit variation. Therefore, we propose a Deep-Q-Network (DQN) based Deep Reinforcement Learning (Deep RL) method to overcome the over-speed problem in various speed limit areas. In this paper, the proposed system will reduce the vehicle speed intelligently if the driver passes over the speed limit in a particular zone. The simulation results show that our proposed solution can successfully reduce the vehicle speed under various zone-based speed limits.

articleTitle: Low-Computation-Cost Data Hiding Scheme Based on 4-2 Double-layer Square Magic Matrix
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Data hiding is a technology of how to embed secret data into digital images. Many combinations of various sizes of doublelayer magic matrix data hiding schemes have been tried. However, the double-layer magic matrix data hiding scheme is high computational complexity. A proposed scheme in this study improves the data hiding scheme of the 4-2 double-layer magic matrix and solves the problem of computational time complexity by changing the range of search elements. Experiment results verify that the proposed scheme speeds up the calculation time and maintains the same hiding capacity.

articleTitle: Survival Prediction in Patients with Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma Using Logistic and Neural Network Models
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: In this study, we used traditional machine learning methods, LR (logistic regression) and RF (random forest), to predict the clinical survival of the patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. We also used the famous SVM (support vector machine) and DNN (deep neural network) models in order to further compare their performances. There were 122 eligible patients included as the dataset. The 3-year OS for all patients was 59.8%. With a deep neural network model, three input variables (SUV of tumor, SUV of biopsy site, and serum level of lactate dehydrogenase) yielded the most outperforming accuracy level. The accuracy scores were also listed and compared in this study.

articleTitle: Learning Risk Prediction Model Based on Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: This paper continuously tracks the learning process of students in the past two years, collects students' learning data, selects data analysis methods and tools, and uses the SVR algorithm to establish a prediction model of students' academic performance for predicting students' academic performance, students' learning behavior and basic characteristics.

articleTitle: Current Problems, Recent Advances and Future Trends in the Design and Manufacturing of Blood Glucose Monitoring Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: The implementation of CPS to the design of BGMS interconnects the uses of glucose meters, test strips, and control solutions with the manufacturing systems through cyberspace to enhance the safety and performance of the BGMS. Furthermore, the implementation of CPS to the manufacturing of BGMS interconnects sensors and information feedbacks from different work stations. This allows the manufacturing systems to be self-aware, self-adaptable, and self-configurable, to reduce manpower, defective rate and production downtime for better productivity.

articleTitle: Research and Development of Synchronous Monitoring for Weight Discrimination and Arrangement Control System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: This study aims to combine the technologies of virtual reality and human machine interface for the application to the practical training of mechatronics machines to help users’ practical learning of mechatronics without restrictions to time and space. Mechatronics machines in schools are limited that learners have to take turns for operation learning in the practical training. It results in extremely long practice time. The self-designed human machine interface integrated virtual reality is applied to the online to offline monitoring of mechatronics machines in order to solve the teaching problems in machines.A 3D model of mechatronics machines is first established and then attached with materials and assembled in this study. The virtual reality software is further used for establishing the virtual scene and machine motion. The human machine interface is finally programmed to monitor and control the virtual reality machine and the physical machine. Leaners, through the offline model on the human machine interface, could learn various device names of machine, operation procedures, and the edition and design of control programs. Through the online model on the human machine interface, leaners could also learn the remote online to offline synchronous monitoring of virtual and real machines. The experimental results reveal that leaners, through offline learning, could rapidly familiarize the operation of real machines and the writing and design of control programs. It would reduce the training time and costs and personnel injury or machine damage caused by leaners’ careless operation or control program errors.

articleTitle: Efficient Deep Learning-driven Approach for PM2.5 Forecasting at Different Locations in Spain
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 3rd Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Forecasting dust pollution is necessary for achieving satisfactory air quality. This work proposes an improved deep learning-based forecasting approach for PM2.5 concentration forecasting. Importantly, this approach introduces an improved variational autoencoder (VAE) model by incorporating a bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU) at the encoder side of the VAE model. The forecasting quality of the coupled model is verified via comparisons with the traditional VAE model when forecasting PM2.5 concentration time-series data. The assessment is carried out using five statistical metrics. PM2.5 datasets from different stations in Spain are used in this study. Results reveal the accuracy of the improved VAE model for PM2.5 concentration forecasting over the traditional VAE, LSTM, GRU, biLSTM, and BiGRU.
